summary.text: Amanda Paliouras is standing as an independent for Bulleen at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Wikipedia's election pages record a candidate of the same name as the Liberal candidate for Preston at the 2022 state election, an Independent Liberal in Manningham's Ruffey Ward at the 2024 council elections, and the Trumpet of Patriots candidate for Menzies at the 2025 federal election; no source we found confirms this is the same person. The ABC's guide gives no biography and links only to a Facebook page as at 9 Nov 2026.

summary.text: Bradley Harvey is the Family First candidate for Bulleen at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he has spent 24 years in surgical technical support in public and private hospitals around Melbourne and regional Victoria, worked for four years helping skilled migrants, and organises political volunteers in northern Melbourne. A Family First candidate of the same name stood for Cranbourne at the 2022 state election.

prior_roles.role: Support work with skilled migrants (four years)

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Bradley Harvey as the Family First candidate; no source says he is the 2026 Bulleen candidate, though the name and party match.

priorities.text: Traditional family values as the basis of a stable, prosperous future

summary.text: Dimitrios (Dimitri) Tafidis is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Bulleen at the 2026 Victorian election. He moved to Australia from Greece in 2016, has a degree in exercise physiology from Deakin University, and works in construction with a fencing firm. A Dimitrios Tafidis also stood for the Victorian Socialists in Manningham's Bolin Ward at the 2024 council elections, though no source seen confirms it is the same person.

occupation.text: Construction worker with a fencing company

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's 2024 results list a Victorian Socialists candidate of this name; no source seen links him to the 2026 Bulleen candidate.

priorities.text: A better world is possible; we only need to reach for it.
More public transport and free community spaces in the Bulleen district
Politics that serves working people rather than billionaires and corporations

summary.text: Greg Rublee is standing as an independent for Bulleen at the 2026 Victorian election, describing himself as a teal independent. Brought up in the Ozarks region of the United States, he moved to Australia in 2011 and took out citizenship in 2016. He is a library business partner at Monash University; his earlier career took in US federal government work in national security, science teaching in a secondary school, and service as a city councillor in Oldsmar, Florida.

prior_roles.role: US federal government roles in national security, budgeting and legislative affairs
Founder and leader, Catch Your Breath (program for neurodiverse young people)

priorities.text: fight for the principles of open, accountable government that all Victorians deserve
Independents holding the balance of power so that legislation gets proper scrutiny
Full public school funding to the agreed standard well ahead of 2034
New public dental clinics, with walk-in care, in regional and high-need communities
Discharge lounges to ease ambulance ramping at hospitals

summary.text: Mahdi Athari is One Nation's candidate for Bulleen at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC, he has more than 23 years of rail engineering and consulting behind him, and his own small business matches railway professionals with work. He migrated from Iran under the skilled migration program in 2013 and has lived in Melbourne since 2015. One Nation's candidate page refused automated access, so it could not be checked.

occupation.text: Rail engineer and consultant; small business owner

prior_roles.role: Engineer and consultant in the rail industry
Owner of a small business connecting railway professionals

summary.text: Matthew Guy is the Liberal member for Bulleen, which he has held since 2014 after eight years in the Legislative Council for Northern Metropolitan Region. He was Minister for Planning from 2010 to 2014 and led the Liberal Party in opposition twice, from 2014 to 2018 and from 2021 to 2022. He is now Shadow Minister for Public Transport and is standing again in Bulleen in 2026.

occupation.text: Political staffer and government relations manager

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Transition to Government
Shadow Minister for Ports and Freight
Minister for Multicultural Affairs and Citizenship

prior_roles.note: Wikipedia gives the start year only.

prior_roles.role: Chief of staff to Denis Napthine (Opposition Leader)
Director of research, office of Premier Jeff Kennett

legal_and_integrity.text: The Victorian Ombudsman investigated his 2011 decision as Planning Minister to rezone farmland at Ventnor, Phillip Island.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: The Ombudsman held him responsible for the rezoning and found he had withheld documents the investigation asked for.

legal_and_integrity.text: He referred himself to IBAC after reports of a dinner with a man police had alleged in court was a senior organised crime figure.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: IBAC said it had no power to investigate.

legal_and_integrity.text: Fined for breaching face mask rules at an event in Parliament House, with four other Coalition MPs.

summary.text: Tomas Lightbody is the Greens candidate for Bulleen at the 2026 Victorian election. A transport and land use planner who has taught urban planning at the University of Melbourne, he sat on Manningham City Council for the Manna Ward from 2020 to 2024 and was deputy mayor in 2022-23. He ran for the Greens at the 2023 Warrandyte by-election and lost his council seat at the 2024 local elections.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists him as the Greens councillor for Manna Ward for 2020-2024; no source seen describes the 2020 election itself.

priorities.text: Better public transport, climate action and cost-of-living relief
